input_messages.content: Hi there. My phone has been saying "No Service" for the past few hours, and I’m not sure what to do. I mostly use it for calls and texts, so I’m a bit worried. Can you help me get it working again?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Let me know if you need anything else.

Oh, I see. So that’s why my phone isn’t working. I didn’t realize my contract had ended. I really just need a simple plan for calls and texts—nothing fancy. Can you help me set up a new plan? I’m not very good with all this, so please keep it simple for me.

I’d really like to keep my current phone number if that’s possible. And I want to use the same phone—I’m comfortable with it, and I don’t want to change devices. Is it possible to keep my number even though my contract ended?
Yes, I’d like to keep my current phone number and use the same device. The Basic Plan sounds good to me—I don’t really use much data, so that should be enough. What do I need to do next?

Oh, I see. So I’ll need to call or go to the store to get this sorted out? That makes me a bit nervous, but I guess I don’t have much choice. Thank you for explaining everything to me. I don’t have any other questions right now.
Thank you for your help and patience. I’ll try to get this sorted out soon. Have a nice day! ###STOP###

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
